newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy studies help for beleaguered car industry.
newsitem.headline: Italy studies help for beleaguered car industry.

text.p: Italy is studying measures to help its car industry which has suffered from a depressed domestic market throughout most of the 1990s, Italy's Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi said on Tuesday.

"The government is studying intervention in the car industry, even of a fiscal nature," Fantozzi said while attending the Turin car show, but he added that no government decisions on this matter are imminent.

The news sent shares in Italy's giant car maker Fiat spinning higher as the stock closed up 4.73 percent at 4,585 lire after the shares had languished in negative territory in early trading on the Milan bourse.

"Intervention is needed for the car industry, whether of a financial and fiscal nature or in the form of investment," Fantozzi said, but he added: "In any case the eventual incentives are not under my control. It is the finance minister who must decide this."

Italy is Europe's fourth largest car market and has remained depressed since the European car market hit a low point in 1993, although most other major European car markets including Germany, France and Britain have all recovered from 1993 levels.

Fiat which has a near half share of the Italian car market has suffered from demand which stubbornly refuses to pick up, although it continues to increase its market share in other European nations with a string of recent new car launches.

The Turin-based group announced results for the first nine months of 1996 late on Monday showing sales up four percent but pre-tax profits slipping 36 percent as it suffered from the depressed Italian car market and the higher value of the lira which is penalising car exports from Italy.
